E1.evidence: The issue gives a fuzz harness, a crashing YAML input and an ASan report: "==18==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x7bb86e3eb94f" ... "#1 0x5619587e6dbc in add_name_to_ns"; maintainer Barry-Xu-2018 confirms and fixes it in rcl PR #1281 ("Fixes https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1777").

units_identified: reporter's libFuzzer harness linking rcl_yaml_param_parser with stubbed rmw_validate_* functions
E2.evidence: The out-of-bounds read is inside the parser's own namespace bookkeeping. Reporter: "it stems from an internal invariant mismatch between `rem_name_from_ns()` and `add_name_to_ns()`". Fix PR: "When add_name_to_ns() is called for the first time and the input `name` is an empty string (\"\" as a key in YAML), it will be directly added to \"ns_tracker->node_ns\". While add_name_to_ns() is called for the second time, `cur_ns` is from ns_tracker->node_ns (it is an empty string). So `ns_len` is 0. `sep_len` is 1 (fixed value). `cur_ns + ns_len - sep_len` caused a pointer out-of-bounds error." The resolving edit is an input check inside the parser: "-  if (NULL == name) {\n+  if (NULL == name || strlen(name) == 0) {" (https://github.com/ros2/rcl/pull/1281). With the real rmw validation functions the input is rejected before this point; the overflow was reached only with the reporter's permissive stubs, which are not a correct rmw peer.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the harness passes a YAML file to the library API: "(void)rcl_parse_yaml_file(filename, params);".

E4.evidence: ASan-detected heap-buffer-overflow (read) in add_name_to_ns, observed only under the fuzz harness: "The **heap-buffer-overflow** is triggered when `rcl_yaml_param_parser` is used with **permissive `rmw_\*` stubs**" (https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1777).

notes: Reporter's revision: "ROS version or commit hash: 90f18f394633f58d4097f318a01bb1c246898c91" (a ros2/ros2 rolling repos-file commit; the maintainer notes each repository there is only pinned to the rolling branch). In a normal deployment the maintainer could not reproduce the overflow and instead got "node name must not be empty, at /root/ros2_latest_src/src/ros2/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/parse.c:492"; the reporter agrees: "With **real** `rmw_validate_*` in a normal ROS 2 deployment, invalid node names / namespaces are rejected and the parser returns an error. In that configuration, this heap-buffer-overflow appears **unreachable**." One could read the case as rcl_yaml_param_parser relying on rmw's name validation to reject empty node names, but the peer in the failing composition is a permissive test stub that does not implement that validation, so the failure does not arise from a mismatch between two correct units; the fix hardens the parser internally.
